purpose: No analyzer may NAME something with a placeholder literal. When a fallback has nothing truthful to say the honest state is ABSENCE, not the string "unknown" — a literal in a name-bearing field becomes a symbol (or edge endpoint) that does not exist in the source. Registered like the regex debt: entries are keyed by source statement (not line, because positions move on every edit and statements do not) with an exact count, so an added site and a deleted one are both deliberate acts.

ooTarget.note: Owner standard: the seven OO lanes must reach zero. The paydown is lane work with fixtures and mutants, not a register edit. R7 meanwhile makes the class un-recurrable (a new site, or a new site at a registered statement, fails the gate) and forbids a registered site from vanishing without a deliberate shrink.

runtimeOwed: STATIC ONLY SO FAR, and the gap is now measured lane by lane rather than disclosed in the abstract. The census proves a source site exists and what shape it has; it does not prove the site fires, and it does not prove that no EMITTED row carries a placeholder. script/m14/tmp/cs-placeholder-runtime-probe.ts walks every emitted name-bearing field (symbol name, ownerName, parameter name, relationship source/target, import module) over a real corpus draw and convicts a value only when the FILE DOES NOT WRITE IT — the first two runs convicting 154 `Null` and 22 `Unknown`/`Anonymous` values were all real members of powershell and fsharp, which is why a value-only runtime rule is not trustworthy. Measured: csharp 0 fabricated names over 300 files (powershell 150 + fsharp 150), so this lane's `|| "anonymous"` fallbacks (15 sites) never fire on real code. The other lanes are still static-only, and each needs its own draw before the class can be called closed at runtime.

shrunkBy.note: The removal is real but the LIVE census count did not move, because a NEW site landed in the c lane in the same window (real-c-analyzer.ts:2494, `parameters.push({ name: "unknown", … })`, arriving with the c lane's #917 commits). The gate convicts it by KEY rather than by count — which is exactly why both halves exist: the count test alone would have seen 49 -> 49 and called it unchanged.
shrunkBy.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/csharp/param-type-honesty (lane 9/9) + mutation-csharp-unknown-parameter-type (0 -> 1 failure) + mutation-csharp-parameter-name-as-type (0 -> 1) + mutation-csharp-varargs-parameter-dropped (0 -> 1) + mutation-csharp-blank-parameter-name (0 -> 1), each caught by that fixture alone. The site's two reachable arms were measured first (script/m14/tmp/cs-param-type-probe.ts: `void M(int a, b)` published type `"b"` — the parameter's own NAME — and 0 of 12,946 parameters over a 400-file powershell draw ever reached either arm on well-formed code), and the fix's own new code was measured the same way (script/m14/tmp/cs-param-noname-tree.ts: `void M(params int[])` published `{ name: "" }`, a blank from the grammar's recovery identifier).

PROVEN UNREACHABLE rather than fixed blind, because the two are different findings: script/m14/tmp/py-module-unknown-probe.ts drives 19 shapes through the analyzer and shows that every parse yielding an `import_from_statement` hands the handler a named child for the module (the module on well-formed input, the imported ITEM on damaged input — `from import c` publishes module `c`), while every shape that would leave `moduleName` empty (`from`, `from . import`, `from (`) produces no import_from_statement node at all. The fallback had no reachable state behind it, so it is now an absence: the import row is still published (its items are real names) with `module` omitted, and the `module:item` relationship — which needs a module to have a target — is emitted only when there is one. No fixture can reach it and no mutant can inject it, so the probe IS the evidence; the same treatment the php lane's two unreachable markers got.

csharp.note: Every name-shaped literal the lane emitted (`Unknown`, `Anonymous`, `Null`) is written in the file that emitted it. The 15 `|| "anonymous"` fallbacks in the analyzer are therefore damaged-tree paths, not live fabrications — the measurement the owner decision about widening the marker rule needed.
